# relationship party

- **CURIE:** [`gmeow:relationshipParty`](gmeow-relationshipParty.md)
- **IRI:** <https://blackcatinformatics.ca/gmeow/relationshipParty>
- **Category:** property
- **Defined by:** [`gmeow:slices/contacts`](../../slices/contacts.md)
- **Box roles:** [RBox role](../boxes/rbox.md) ([What is this?](../../four-boxes/index.md))

An agent who is one of the parties to an interpersonal relationship. Non-functional: a relationship typically binds two parties (and is left open for group ties).

## Structure

**Property shape:** object property; [`gmeow:InterpersonalRelationship`](../classes/gmeow-InterpersonalRelationship.md) -> [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md)

## Practical Pattern

Use [`gmeow:relationshipParty`](gmeow-relationshipParty.md) from [`gmeow:InterpersonalRelationship`](../classes/gmeow-InterpersonalRelationship.md) to [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md) when the relationship itself belongs in the native GMEOW graph.

## Common Companion Terms

[`gmeow:InterpersonalRelationship`](../classes/gmeow-InterpersonalRelationship.md), [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md)

## Usage Advice

### Use when

- Use to bind each agent that takes part in an interpersonal-relationship relator; at least one party is required by axiom.

### Avoid when

- Avoid forcing exactly two parties at the OWL level (it is non-functional and left open for group ties; the two-party constraint is a SHACL closure concern) and avoid using it on the flat shortcut edges, which bind their agents directly.

### How to use

- Attach each participating [`gmeow:Agent`](../classes/gmeow-Agent.md) to the relator with this property; pair with [`gmeow:relationshipInterval`](gmeow-relationshipInterval.md) to scope the tie in time.

### Examples

- ex:tie [`gmeow:relationshipParty`](gmeow-relationshipParty.md) ex:lillith.
